title: Zero-delta appliance handoff runbook
content:
Purpose:
This note captures a low-risk, zero-delta approach for handing off an on‑prem appliance control plane and runtime during upgrades or migration to a new control plane version. The technique emphasizes state parity (zero-delta), reversible promotion, and Terraform-safe state reconciliation. This is an experimental runbook for larger customer on‑prem upgrades; treat as draft and adapt to site specifics.

Context and constraints:
- Target audience: solutions engineers + SRE + customer infra owner.
- Applies to VPC-connected appliances and single-tenant on‑prem installs where a second appliance can be brought online for shadowing.
- Goal: perform an in-place upgrade/migration that results in zero perceptible delta in API surface/behavior for callers and no data loss.
- Must respect customers' TF state constraints and minimize changes to resource addresses.

High-level strategy (phases):
1) PREPARE: validate, baseline, and create an isolated shadow appliance.
   - Take thorough baselines: metrics snapshot (p90/p99 latency, error-rate), KV store head hashes, active sessions counts, and model cache sizes. Store baseline artifacts in customer S3/GCS or encrypted share.
   - Verify Terraform state health and locks. If state has drift or manual edits, reconcile before proceeding (see TF reconciliation checklist below).
   - Provision a shadow appliance in the same network (VPC peering/VPN route), but isolated in a different TF workspace or brand-new resource addresses that will later be aliased. The shadow will run the new control-plane/runtime version.

2) MIRROR: mirror control-plane traffic and KV/state changes (eventually consistent).
   - Enable write-forwarding shim on primary: every control-plane write is forwarded to shadow via a resilient queue (Kafka or SQS). Reads continue to hit primary.
   - Deploy a lightweight state syncer that consumes the queue and applies writes idempotently to the shadow's KV store. Use versioned apply with optimistic locking to avoid overwriting newer primary writes.
   - Run contract tests continuously against the shadow's API (read-only and synthetic write flows) to ensure parity. Track divergence alerts if any contract fails for >5m.

3) VERIFY: run in-shadow canaries and correctness checks.
   - Run read-only traffic split (1-2%): route a small percentage of live requests to the shadow in canary mode and compare response digests. For deterministic endpoints, compare full payloads. For non-deterministic text, use semantic equivalence checks and token-level distributions.
   - Run model-serving KV cache checks: ensure shadow's KV cache warm-up converges to expected hit rate within configured window.
   - Check observability parity: tracing correlation between primary and shadow, ensure logs contain identical request ids.

4) SWITCHOVER (zero-delta promotion): pin, alias, and promote without changing client addresses.
   - Acquire TF state lock. Prepare a maintenance window but leave it short; most work is behind smaller fences.
   - Promote the shadow control plane by performing the following atomic steps:
     a) Ingress gateway aliasing: update the load-balancer/TCP proxy to point the customer-facing VIP to the shadow edge (use weighted switch to 100% in one-step if network supports immediate cut).
     b) Promote KV: apply one final flush-forward to ensure the shadow has applied all outstanding queued writes. Verify kv-hash equality.
     c) Update service-discovery TTLs and health-check gating to shift traffic.
   - Keep the original appliance online as read-only fallback for at least a configurable grace period (default 30 minutes) and continue mirroring writes from promoted shadow back to original to avoid data loss on rollback.

5) OBSERVE and STABILIZE:
   - Monitor core SLOs: latency p50/p95/p99, error rate, model response divergences, and CPU/GPU utilization for 60 minutes.
   - Run automated regression tests and sample user flows. If any safety thresholds breach (see rollback triggers) begin rollback.

6) FINALIZE: TF state reconciliation and housekeeping.
   - If permanent, readdress Terraform resources to keep a single source of truth: either import the promoted shadow resources under original TF addresses using terraform import scripts, or perform a controlled rename with state moves.
   - Document and tag the state change in the customer's TF backend with a short note and the runbook run id.
   - Drain and decommission the old appliance only after 24–72h of healthy metrics.

Terraform module notes (practical tips):
- Workspaces vs. addresses: prefer creating a shadow with different resource addresses (e.g., append -shadow) to avoid accidental tf state overwrite. Once promoted, use terraform state mv to move resources into the canonical address.
- Locking: ensure strong backend locking (DynamoDB for S3 backend, Cloud SQL row lock, etc.). Never run parallel terraform apply on both appliances.
- Import scripts: provide idempotent bash/python scripts that call terraform import and then terraform state rm on temp placeholders. Log every import action to the run log.
- Resource drift detection: run `terraform plan` pre/post steps and fail fast on unexpected drifts. For stateful DBs, compare schema hashes rather than relying only on TF output.

API compatibility guidance and gating tests:
- Always run contract tests from the customer's test harness against both control planes. Include API schema checks, response status code distribution, and header invariants.
- Add integration cases for function/tool-calling endpoints and streaming endpoints (partial-response reconciliation).
- Implement a header-based version gate: clients can opt into the new behavior via an X-RW-Preview header to exercise new control-plane endpoints before the cutover.

Rollback decision matrix (triggers and actions):
- Trigger thresholds (any triggers lead to immediate rollback):
  - Error rate increase: baseline error-rate * 3 sustained > 5 minutes.
  - Latency regression: p99 > baseline p99 + 350ms for 10 minutes.
  - Data divergence: KV head-hash mismatch or missing events > 0 after final flush.
  - Model quality regression: automated eval score delta > configured threshold for production prompts.
- Immediate rollback action list:
  1) Switch LB back to original appliance (VIP swap).
  2) Re-enable bidirectional mirroring (ensure writes on current live are forwarded to fallback).
  3) Mark run as "rollback-executed" and capture incident artifacts (metrics, traces, last-kv-diff).
  4) Open a post-mortem ticket and tag eng/private-deployments and product L3.

Edge cases and mitigation notes:
- Partial TF move failure: if terraform state mv fails for some resources, keep both appliances running while you resolve resource-level conflicts. Do not delete any appliance until state reconciles.
- Network flakiness during promotion: use health-check grace periods and consider staged weight moves (80/20 then 100) if your LB supports weighted routing to avoid abrupt TCP resets.
- External integrations with fixed IP allowlists: pre-coordinate allowlist update windows or support inbound proxying so client IPs do not change.

Runbook checklist (quick):
- [ ] Baseline metrics captured and uploaded
- [ ] TF state validated and locked
- [ ] Shadow appliance provisioned and reachable
- [ ] Write-forwarding shim enabled and queue healthy
- [ ] Contract tests green for 30m
- [ ] Canary traffic 1–2% comparing digests
- [ ] KV head-hash parity verified
- [ ] Maintenance window and owner on-call declared
- [ ] LB aliasing plan and rollback playbook ready
- [ ] Post-promotion TF import script ready

Commands & snippets (examples):
- Check TF locks: `aws dynamodb get-item --table-name tf-locks --key '{"LockID":{"S":"shared-drives-prod"}}'`
- Export KV head-hash: `curl -s localhost:9000/kv/head-hash | jq -r .hash > /tmp/kv-hash-primary`
- Final flush-forward: `./syncer flush --to shadow --wait 300`
- Import promoted edge: `terraform import module.appliance[0].control_plane aws_instance.appliance-42`

Post-run artifacts to collect (minimum):
- Run id and timestamp, baseline snapshots, final kv-hash, terraform plan outputs pre/post, list of imported resource addresses, canary diff logs, and on-call notes. Upload these to the customer's secure runbook S3 and attach to the JIRA run ticket.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Add automated state-diff tooling that can produce a safe list of resources eligible for `terraform state mv` without manual verification.
- Evaluate using a provider-level aliasing feature (if we can support aliasing resource addresses without state moves) to speed post-promotion cleanup.
- Gains: test this at scale in staging with a 3-node appliance cluster to validate KV convergence windows.

Notes for handoff to Solutions Eng/Customer:
- Provide a one-page TL;DR for customers that highlights network requirements (peering, VIP flexibility), expected maintenance windows, and explicit rollback windows.
- During customer dry-run, exercise the import script against a cloned state to ensure no surprises.

Author note: this is intentionally prescriptive but still experimental. Please add site-specific steps and convert to canonical runbook after a few successful pilot runs.
